subject: Throughput acceptance checklist and demo sync
messages:
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Throughput acceptance checklist and demo sync

Sam —

Thanks again for the demo yesterday. To make the production handoff tidy, we want to run the acceptance exercises outlined below during the next week's window (Mar 6–7). I put a short checklist and proposed schedule together so your SREs know what to expect. Quick ask: can you confirm an endpoint we can hit (staging) and whether your team can participate live for the 45-minute verification?

Acceptance targets (proposed):
- Steady-state throughput: 300 requests/sec sustained for 30 minutes (payload mixture attached).
- P95 latency goal: < 250 ms for generative text endpoints, measured end-to-end.
- Tail tolerance: 99th percentile < 450 ms during steady-state.
- Error rate: < 0.5% 5xx during the test window.

Planned tests:
1) Prefix warmup + KV cache pre-population (10 minutes)
2) Steady-state load (30 minutes)
3) Spike test (3x nominal for 5 minutes)
4) Gradual ramp down and artifact collection (10 minutes)

Redwood will run the stress harness from our dedicated test pool using the exact seed files in the attachment (acme-loadsim-config.yaml). We recommend running the steady-state twice (two separate 30-min runs) if your network or infra scheduling could introduce jitter.

Attachments: redwood-onboard-runbook.pdf (run steps), payloads included in acme-loadsim-config.yaml

If that all looks good, propose we sync Monday 03/06 at 10:00 PT to start the first run. If you prefer a different slot, we can adjust.

Thanks —
Laura
Laura Bennett
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwood.com
+1 415 555 0187

From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme.com>
To: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Platform Team <ops@acme.com>
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput acceptance checklist and demo sync

Laura, thanks — this plan looks reasonable. A few notes from our side after a quick infra sync:

- Staging endpoint: https://staging-api.acme.com/gen (TLS certs are valid)
- Baseline: our current staging steady-state sits around 280–320 req/s depending on payload mix; p95 ~ 270–320 ms (we've seen occasional peaks to ~420 ms under GC events).
- We're good to have two SREs on the call (me + Priya) for the runs.

We attached our load simulator config (acme-loadsim-config.yaml) which contains the payload distribution we typically use for preprod. We will enable packet capture on the staging VIP for the two runs and share telemetry after the test.

Request: please include in your runbook the specific quantization variant and batching window you plan to test (we want to compare default quantized-8 vs unquantized FP16 for this workload). Also please list the Redis/KV cache warmup steps so we can mirror state.

We can do Monday 03/06 at 10:00 PT. Looking forward to the test.

—Sam
Sam Ortiz
Platform Engineer, Acme Retail
sam.ortiz@acme.com

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 6 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput acceptance checklist and demo sync — Redwood run specifics

Sam / team —

Thanks for the quick confirmation and for sharing the staging endpoint. A few specifics from Redwood's execution plan so the telemetry you get is directly comparable to our internal metrics: 

Runbook highlights (we will attach the full PDF to the artifact folder):
- Model variants: we will test two variants in this order — (1) quantized int8 (q8) optimized kernel, (2) FP16 with standard kernel. Each steady-state run will be labeled in telemetry to indicate variant.
- Batching window: 20 ms (continuous batching enabled). We'll run an additional short window at 40 ms if you prefer to see batching sensitivity.
- KV cache prewarm: we will replay the first 5k unique prefixes from the seed set against the model to populate caches for 10 minutes prior to the steady-state run. Please ensure staging replicas are at the same model version tag (v1.3.2).
- Observability: we'll push logs to your collection endpoint and publish per-token latency breakdowns to the Drive folder. Our console will also stream a lightweight trace for each run.
- Failure handling: if error rate exceeds 1% for longer than 3 minutes we abort and capture heap/GC traces.

Artifacts we will produce and share after each run:
- per-run token-level latency CSV (redwood-steady-state-results-20280307.csv)
- consolidated summary PDF with P95/P99/QPS charts
- raw request/response samples (redacted) for QA

We will also create a HubSpot activity HS-10294 and link the artifacts there. After the second successful steady-state run we'll request formal acceptance; acceptance criteria should be the targets Laura outlined but we're happy to formalize with slightly relaxed thresholds if you prefer (e.g., p95 < 300 ms if needed).

I'll be on the call and will own the harness execution. Ben will monitor resource metrics and Karthik will help with kernel/quantization knobs if any tuning is required mid-run.

Call reminder: Mon 03/06, 10:00 PT (meeting link in calendar).

Cheers,
Monica Patel
Onboarding Engineering Lead, Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Attachment: redwood-onboard-runbook.pdf (stub)

From: Sam Ortiz <sam.ortiz@acme.com>
To: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: ACME Platform Team <ops@acme.com>
Date: Tue, 7 Mar 2028 14:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Throughput acceptance checklist and demo sync — Results and provisional sign-off

Monica / Laura —

Thanks for running the tests today. Quick summary of outcomes:

- Steady-state run 1 (q8): sustained 310 req/s, P95 245 ms, P99 430 ms, 5xx 0.12%
- Steady-state run 2 (FP16): sustained 300 req/s, P95 265 ms, P99 460 ms, 5xx 0.10%
- Spike: 3x nominal produced transient P95 up to 520 ms but no outages; error rate remained under 0.4%

We reviewed the artifacts in the Drive folder (https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1qA_demo_acceptance_artifacts). The CSV and summary PDF are there. Given our internal SLAs, we're comfortable provisionally accepting the q8 runs where P95 <= 250 ms. We'll follow up with a short governance ticket to finalize timeline for production rollout.

Acceptance notes: please add the per-route token-cost breakdown in the summary PDF (helps procurement). Once that's added we'll mark the onboarding acceptance as DONE on our side and proceed with the migration cutover plan.

Appreciate the collaboration — nice to see the KV warmup helped smooth the tail.

—Sam
Sam Ortiz
Platform Engineer, Acme Retail

Attachment: redwood-steady-state-results-20280307.csv (stub)
